turns.text: Edward brought round a farewell card on Friday that I need to sign before tomorrow. We've really only ever exchanged morning hellos when handing over deliveries at the front desk, so I want to keep it polite and warm while maintaining the distance appropriate for a counter acquaintance. I'm not really sure how I should word the line or where to start, and someone mentioned choosing a good valediction, but what does that term actually mean?

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text:
Great — let's start with the term, then the card.

**"Valediction"** just means the sign-off at the end of a message — "Best," "Warmly," "All the best," that kind of thing. It's the word you write before your name. The term itself comes from the Latin for "to say farewell."

For Edward — counter acquaintance, only ever exchanged hellos over deliveries — you want something that reads as genuine but doesn't pretend you were close. Short and clean is your friend here.

Something like:

> *Edward — it's been a pleasure having you at the front of the building all this time. Wishing you all the best in your next chapter.*
> 
> *[YOUR NAME]*

**Valediction:** "Warmly" would be fine, though honestly for this level of acquaintance "All the best" sits perfectly — it's friendly without overreaching. If you want it to land slightly warmer, "With appreciation" works too, since you can appreciate someone's presence without being close.

So the full note:

> *Edward — it's been a pleasure having you at the front of the building all this time. Wishing you all the best in your next chapter.*
> 
> *All the best,*
> *[YOUR NAME]*

How's that feel? Want to tweak the tone either way?

turns.text: Defining valediction right at the start and laying out that first step made it really clear where to begin.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text:
Glad that landed right — "valediction" is one of those words you hear but never really stop to think about until you're staring at a blank card, so it felt like the place to start.

So the note I suggested:

> *Edward — it's been a pleasure having you at the front of the building all this time. Wishing you all the best in your next chapter.*
> 
> *All the best,*
> *[YOUR NAME]*

Does that work for you, or would you like to adjust anything — the warmth, the length, maybe swap "pleasure" for something that sounds more like you?
